svg.aria-label: Hang tag specification is five lines: size, stock, print, hole and cord — with the cord as the line most buyers forget

g.text: The specification that travels well is five lines
Size, stock, print, hole — and cord. The cord is the line most buyers forget to ask about
SIZE
2×3 or 2×3.5 apparel standard · 1.5–2″ jewelry · long formats for charts
STOCK
14–16 pt covers most brand tags · 18 pt kraft heavy natural
PRINT
digital full colour · silkscreen solids · foil metallic · one or both sides
HOLE
≈0.15″ (4 mm), centered near top · 5 positions on request
CORD
material · thickness · attachment — its own line, never an assumption
cotton and jute for natural/kraft · finer cords for jewelry ·
elastic loops for tags pulled on and off repeatedly
Where string assumptions die
“Strings are not included with standard orders” (UPrinting);
Vistaprint sells cord separately — a 23-ft cotton or jute rope,
2 mm thick, cutting for about 50 tags.
A stringing lane exists as a service:
· poly/cotton, elastic or natural cords
· knotted — arrives retail-ready, pre-tied at the ends
· looped — the end user ties; labor stays with your team
· strings shipped loose with the order as a third option
Cotton and elastic strings run “in lengths from 2 to 10 inches
from hole to knot”; tags can arrive “drilled and pre-strung”.
Non-standard cord colors carry “higher minimum orders and
extended lead times”; per-piece attaching labor is quoted with
the service, not published — budget it as a finishing line.
Cord supply and options are confirmed in the quotation rather than assumed from a catalog — the five-line spec keeps every party quoting the same tag.
